_comment: MCP servers Uniagent may use. Reached by the model through the `mcp` tool,
never directly - see scripts/mcp_client.py.
A server is declared one of two ways.
1. A PROGRAM Uniagent starts and talks to over its stdin/stdout:
"command"  the program to run. Required for this form.
"args"     its arguments, as a list.
"env"      extra environment variables, as an object.
"cwd"      working directory to start it in.
2. A SERVER ALREADY LISTENING ON A PORT, which Uniagent connects to:
"url"       where it is, e.g. "http://localhost:3001/mcp".
Required for this form. Uniagent does not start it -
whatever is on that port has to be running already.
"transport" OPTIONAL, "http" or "sse". Leave it out and both are
tried, HTTP first: that is the current standard, SSE is
the older one many servers still only speak. So a bare
url is usually enough on its own.
"headers"   OPTIONAL, sent with every request. This is where an
auth token goes, e.g. {"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}.
Either form also takes:
"enabled"  set false to switch a server off without deleting it.
"tools"    OPTIONAL allowlist of tool names, and the most useful
field here. Naming tools does TWO things: it hides the
rest, and it attaches the ones you named to the model as
tools in their own right, called mcp__server__tool and
carrying the server's own argument schema. Those need no
lookup step and their arguments cannot be got wrong.
Leave it out and the whole server sits behind the `mcp`
tool instead: the model has to ask what's there and then
type the arguments itself, but it costs one tool's worth
of context however many tools the server has. Name the
handful you actually use - every tool you name spends its
schema on EVERY request from then on, so a forty-tool
server listed in full is a large standing cost.
"timeout"  OPTIONAL seconds to allow one call, default 60. Raise it
for a server that does slow work, like a build.
The allowlist covers TOOLS only. A server's resources and prompts are
always reached through the `mcp` tool, listed on demand rather than
carried in the prompt, so they cost nothing until something asks for
them and there is no list to keep short.
